title: Elder Bhalliya: “Who drives away the army of Death, As a great flood sweeps away a frail bridge of reeds — Victorious, fearless, Having subdued,…
content:
Elder Bhalliya:
“Who drives away the army of Death,
As a great flood sweeps away a frail bridge of reeds —
Victorious, fearless,
Having subdued, he dwells at peace.”

title: Elder Nun Sumedhā: “What is this foul, stinking body, Frightening, A leather bag full of corpses, Oozing impurities? What is this body I know —…
content:
Elder Nun Sumedhā:

“What is this foul, stinking body,
Frightening,
A leather bag full of corpses,
Oozing impurities?

What is this body I know —
Disgusting, smeared with flesh and blood,
A dwelling for worms,
Food for birds —
This body is like that —
To whom should I give it now?

The body, thrown in a charnel ground,
Not long, loses consciousness —
Like a discarded log —
Relatives are disgusted.

That body thrown in the charnel ground,
Becomes food for others —
Formerly they washed it clean,
Now they are disgusted —
Even parents are like that —
What to say of ordinary people?

They are infatuated with a body without core,
Bound by sinews and bones,
Full of saliva and tears,
Full of feces and urine, foul-smelling.

If this body were cut open,
Its inner parts revealed,
Even one’s mother would be disgusted,
Unable to bear the stench.

It is because of aggregates, elements, and sense-bases
That this body is constituted —
The root of renewed existence, suffering —
They speak of it rightly —
They do not delight in it at all.
So who would I wish to marry?

Even a hundred spears every day,
Constantly piercing the body —
Though harmed for a hundred years —
That would still be better,
Because that suffering,
In the end, would be destroyed.

The wise would agree to such killing,
As the Teacher declared —
They wander on for a long time,
With minds given to killing,
Continually following one after another.

In the realms of devas and humans,
Animals, asuras,
Hungry ghosts, and hell —
They undergo endless slaughter.

In hell, there are many —
Those with defiled minds, fallen —
The heavenly realm is no refuge —
There is no Nibbāna-like happiness there.

Those who attain Nibbāna
Are intimately connected
With the teaching
Of the One with Ten Powers —
At ease, unruffled,
Striving to end birth and death.

Today, father, I am determined to leave.
These empty possessions
Are of no value.
I am disgusted with sensual pleasures,
I am weary of sensual pleasures —
They have been cut off,
Like a palm tree stump.”

title: Then the Blessed One, knowing “This is Māra the Evil One,” recited this verse to Māra: Forms, sounds, tastes, and smells, And all contacts, all…
content:
Then the Blessed One, knowing “This is Māra the Evil One,” recited this verse to Māra:
Forms, sounds, tastes, and smells,
And all contacts, all phenomena —
These are terrifying things,
Bewildering beings in the world.
A disciple of the Perfectly Enlightened One,
Mindful, transcends them all,
Transcending Māra’s power,
Shining like the sun.

title: “Monks, I do not see any other hindrance by which beings, hindered, wander and transmigrate for a long time as this hindrance of ignorance. Monks,…
content:
“Monks, I do not see any other hindrance by which beings, hindered, wander and transmigrate for a long time as this hindrance of ignorance. Monks, hindered by the hindrance of ignorance, beings wander and transmigrate for a long time.

No other thing so hinders beings,
That they run on by day and night,
As that of delusion’s snare.

But one who has abandoned delusion,
Pierced through the mass of darkness,
No longer wanders on —
In them the cause is no more.”

title: “And what, monks, is dwelling heedfully? If one lives without restraint of the eye faculty, monks, his mind is defiled by forms cognizable by the…
content: “And what, monks, is dwelling heedfully? If one lives without restraint of the eye faculty, monks, his mind is defiled by forms cognizable by the eye. For one with a defiled mind, there is no gladness. Without gladness, there is no rapture. Without rapture, there is no tranquility. Without tranquility, suffering remains. For one who is suffering, the mind does not become concentrated. When the mind is not concentrated, phenomena are not clearly seen. When phenomena are not clearly seen, he is called ‘one who dwells heedfully’ … the ear faculty … the nose faculty … the tongue faculty … the body faculty … If one lives without restraint of the mind faculty, his mind is defiled by phenomena cognizable by the mind. For one with a defiled mind, there is no gladness … he is called ‘one who dwells heedfully.’ Thus, monks, is dwelling heedfully.”

title: Elder Añña-Koṇḍañña: I am exceedingly joyful, Having heard the supreme Dhamma, The Dhamma taught for dispassion, Completely without clinging. In this world of a round…
content:
Elder Añña-Koṇḍañña:

I am exceedingly joyful,
Having heard the supreme Dhamma,
The Dhamma taught for dispassion,
Completely without clinging.

In this world of a round earth,
With many colors and forms,
Bewildering the mind —
Thus I thought:
The sign of beauty is very enticing,
Connected with lust.

As wind blows away dust,
As rain settles it down,
Thoughts become stilled
When seen with wisdom.

All conditioned things are impermanent —
When seen with wisdom,
One becomes disenchanted with suffering —
This is the path to purity.

All conditioned things are suffering —
When seen with wisdom,
One becomes disenchanted with suffering —
This is the path to purity.

All phenomena are not-self —
When seen with wisdom,
One becomes disenchanted with suffering —
This is the path to purity.

title: “Monks, short indeed is the lifespan of humans in this world — one must go on to the future. Do good, live the holy life.…
content:
“Monks, short indeed is the lifespan of humans in this world — one must go on to the future. Do good, live the holy life. For nothing that is born is without death. Monks, a long-lived person lives only a hundred years, or a little more or less.

Human life is short,
The good person should be concerned,
Live as if the head is on fire —
Death will surely come.

Days and nights pass by,
Life span comes to an end,
Human life dries up
Like a stream in the mountains.”

title: Who has conquered the thorn of sensuality, Insult, injury, bondage, That one stands firm, Like a mountain unshaken — Such a monk, Pleasure and pain…
content:
Who has conquered the thorn of sensuality,
Insult, injury, bondage,
That one stands firm,
Like a mountain unshaken —
Such a monk,
Pleasure and pain do not disturb.

title: “Form, sound, taste, smell, touch — All these things Are desirable, delightful, agreeable As long as they exist. The world with its devas Regards them…
content:
“Form, sound, taste, smell, touch —
All these things
Are desirable, delightful, agreeable
As long as they exist.

The world with its devas
Regards them as delightful,
But when they cease,
Then they are seen as suffering.

The noble ones see as happiness
The destruction of identity.
This is completely opposite
To what the whole world sees.

What others call happiness,
The noble call suffering.
What others call suffering,
The noble know as happiness.

The good have open eyes, they see, they have light —
Apart from the noble ones,
Who is worthy of perfect enlightenment?
By that right knowledge of the path,
They attain Nibbāna, free from defilements.”

title: “Monks, there are these four noble searches. What four? Here, monks, a person being himself subject to aging, having known the peril in what is…
content: “Monks, there are these four noble searches. What four? Here, monks, a person being himself subject to aging, having known the peril in what is subject to aging, seeks the unaging, supreme security from bondage, Nibbāna; being himself subject to sickness, having known the peril in sickness, seeks the unailing, supreme security from bondage, Nibbāna; being himself subject to death, having known the peril in death, seeks the deathless, supreme security from bondage, Nibbāna; being himself subject to defilement, having known the peril in defilement, seeks the undefiled, supreme security from bondage, Nibbāna. These, monks, are the four noble searches.”
